## The assignment

All participants complete this as their final project, in **teams of
three**. [`Day5_Lab.ipynb`](Day5_Lab.ipynb) is your starter template — a
five-module pipeline that already runs end to end, on purpose, so you can
verify your environment before extending it. Your team's actual deliverable
is to replace its lightweight stand-ins with the real tools from the week.

## What the starter already does

The notebook wires together a DAG of five modules over a synthetic
e-commerce order stream:

| Module | Stage | What the starter uses |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ingestion | `MockKafka` — an in-memory producer/topic/offset simulator |
| 2 | Storage | Bronze / Silver / Gold Lakehouse, written with pandas + Parquet |
| 3 | Quality Gate | Five hand-rolled DAMA-style checks (completeness, accuracy, uniqueness, validity, timeliness) |
| 4 | Serving | A RAG pipeline over the Gold layer, using an in-memory ChromaDB collection and `sentence-transformers` |
| 5 | Orchestration | A DAG executor that runs modules 1–4 in dependency order and emits JSON lineage events |

It's deliberately built from lightweight stand-ins — `MockKafka` instead of a
real broker, pandas/Parquet instead of Delta Lake, hand-rolled checks instead
of Great Expectations — so it runs anywhere with no external services and
you can confirm your environment works before touching real infrastructure.

## What's actually graded: the extension checklist

Your team's job is to replace each stand-in with the real library you
already used earlier in the week. This checklist is also printed at the end
of every run of the notebook:

| Replace | With | Reference implementation |
|---|---|---|
| `MockKafka` | a real `kafka-python` producer/consumer | Day 2's Kafka lab |
| pandas Parquet writes | PySpark + Delta Lake | Day 1's Delta Lake lab |
| the five manual checks | Great Expectations checkpoints | Day 4's quality gate lab |
| `chromadb.Client()` (in-memory) | a persistent Chroma instance or Pinecone | Day 3's RAG lab |
| `module5_orchestrate()`'s task calls | tasks wrapped in a real Airflow DAG | [Orchestrating the platform](01_unified_architecture.qmd#orchestrating-the-platform) |
| — (new) | an OpenLineage HTTP emitter pointing at a Marquez server | Day 4's lineage lab |
| — (new) | a recorded 10-minute demo covering all five modules | — |

If your team gets stuck on any single item, that day's lab notebook has a
working reference call for the real library — the starter's mock exists
specifically so you can see the *shape* of what needs replacing before you
go find the real API.

## Deliverables and rubric

| Deliverable | Requirement | Points |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Ingestion layer | Kafka producer + consumer with schema validation | 20 |
| 2. Delta Lakehouse | Bronze/Silver/Gold zones with `MERGE` and schema enforcement | 25 |
| 3. RAG pipeline | Chunking, embedding, vector index, hybrid search with reranking | 25 |
| 4. Orchestration | Airflow DAG connecting all modules end-to-end | 15 |
| 5. Quality gate | Great Expectations suite + OpenLineage events emitted | 15 |
| **Total** | | **100** |

Submission is a GitHub repository with a README documenting the
architecture and how to run it.

::: {.callout-note}
This mirrors the course's standing capstone rubric exactly (100 points,
ingestion / lakehouse / RAG / orchestration / quality-and-lineage), because
Day 5's final project **is** the capstone submission for this course — not a
separate practice exercise.
:::

## Framing your submission

The deck also sketches four illustrative real-world scenarios this same
five-layer pattern maps onto — a real-time customer-support intelligence
platform, a healthcare clinical-trial matcher, an academic research
aggregator with a citation graph, and an e-commerce product Q&A system. Your
team isn't required to build one of these specifically; the actual deliverable
is the checklist above applied to the starter's e-commerce order dataset. But
if your README benefits from a concrete "who would use this and why," picking
one of these framings for your write-up is a reasonable way to motivate the
architecture you built, without changing what's graded.

## Setup and running

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Only install the extension dependencies for the specific real tools your
team is integrating (Kafka, Delta Lake, Great Expectations, Airflow, etc.) —
you don't need all of them at once to get started. Open
[`Day5_Lab.ipynb`](Day5_Lab.ipynb) and run all cells top to bottom; the first
code cell installs the starter's own dependencies via `!pip install`.

Output lands in:

- `./lakehouse/bronze/` — raw ingested records
- `./lakehouse/silver/` — cleansed, validated records
- `./lakehouse/gold/` — revenue aggregation by country
- `./lineage_events/` — the pipeline's JSON audit trail

::: {.callout-note}
Module 4's `SentenceTransformerEmbeddingFunction` downloads the
`all-MiniLM-L6-v2` model from the Hugging Face Hub the first time it runs —
this needs internet access on that first run (in Colab or locally); the
model is cached afterward and subsequent runs are offline. On Windows, the
Hugging Face cache also falls back to a non-symlinked copy of the model
files instead of symlinks, which just uses a little more disk space — it
does not affect correctness.
:::

## Standing project requirements — every SDAIA Academy capstone

On top of this course's rubric, every project in every SDAIA Academy program
must additionally satisfy the following, and it's part of how the project is
evaluated:

- Every trainee must **create and activate a GitHub account**, if they don't
  already have one.
- The project must be **uploaded to GitHub**, kept documented, and
  continuously updated.
- The repository must include:
  - A clear, comprehensive **project description**
  - A **professional README** — the project idea plus how to run/use it
  - Proper **technical documentation**
  - Good **Git version-control practices** — meaningful, incremental
    commits; a sane repository structure; a `.gitignore` excluding secrets
    and generated files
  - A statement of **which training program** the project was completed
    under (program name and cohort dates)
  - A link to **SDAIA Academy's GitHub** — <https://github.com/SDAIAAcademy>
    — where relevant

Encouraged, though not scored: support outstanding Saudi projects on
GitHub — star high-quality repositories, follow Saudi accounts and
repositories, contribute to open source, engage via forks, pull requests, and
issues, and share standout projects with the wider tech community.
